notes: This file is authored campaign data. A generator will translate it to Cobblemon native dialogue pages, Molang predicates, and server actions.
Dialogue never owns mutable quest state. Conditions and actions reference progression fields declared by the quest contract.
The dialogue cursor is a first-class per-player progression field, not transient UI state.
A conversation with npc_id null has no NPC: a prop or an actor in data/scenes.json opens it for the player who clicked.
An optional speakers map names each speaker; a speaker mapped to null is narration and its page names nobody.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Before you ask: no.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: No what? Exactly.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: I am just a traveler with a familiar face.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: People see the bandana and lose all judgment.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: All eyes on me. Constant problem.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: You got any supplies?

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Something clear. Cool. Life-supporting.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Not that I need water.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: I could stop being thirsty whenever I want.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: I am choosing not to.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Builds character.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Also headaches.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Things change when you have not had a drink all day.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Keep your head up. Mine is pounding.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Again: I am not asking for water.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: I am creating an opportunity for generosity.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Different thing.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: And I am not Tupac.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Never heard of him.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Water first. Questions never.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Well?

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: You got any supplies?

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: I could stop being thirsty whenever I want.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Again: I am not asking for water.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Water first. Questions never.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: A whole bucket.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: I asked for water, not municipal infrastructure.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Still counts.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Here. Take your bucket back.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: That is exactly what I was not asking for.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Hand it over.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Finally.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: All right. You helped me. I respect that.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: You want the truth?

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Fine. People used to call me Pac.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: That is all you are getting.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Tell nobody where this hut is.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Especially anybody carrying a camera.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: I have had enough eyes on me.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Take these. Payment for the water and the silence.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: If anyone asks, you met a handsome beekeeper.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: I do not own bees. That helps the story.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Handsome beekeeper. Remember the story.

nodes.speaker: stranger
nodes.text: Prepared now, huh? Growth.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: My wife is in there.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: I woke up outside. Just outside. No idea how.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: One second, kitchen. Next second, grass in my mouth.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: And my chud wife is still inside.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Lena! If you hear me, yell something rude!

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Nothing. That is actually unusual.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: She normally has something ready.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: We were fighting when it happened.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Not a serious fight.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Well. It had become serious to her.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: It started with a spoon.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: A completely normal spoon.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: I put it in the wrong drawer.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Apparently we have a correct spoon drawer.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: She was being a total fungus about it.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Very fungal behavior.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: The chud heard me say that.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: She always hears me say that.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: My chud wife loves rules nobody voted on.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Forks left. Spoons right. I get tires sometimes...

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Then she brought up the boots.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: The boots were by the door.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: "Doors are where boots go." chud ahhhh shit yk twin.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: The chud says boots go under the bench.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: The bench is also by the door.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: We agree geographically.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Philosophically, we are enemies.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Then the windows flashed purple.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: I thought the chud had finally become psychic.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: She said, “Hank, that is not me.”

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Very calm for a fungus. Suspiciously calm.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: The floor pulled sideways.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Not down. Sideways.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Floors should pick one direction.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: The cupboard opened.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Every correct spoon became airborne.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: I was struck by her entire argument.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Three spoons. Maybe four.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: She laughed.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: During a disaster, the chud laughed at me. Crazy work.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: That is my chud, though.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: She finds the exact wrong moment delightful.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: I tried to grab the table.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: The table left first.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: If you find it, the left leg wobbles.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Do not let that chud pretend it does not.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: She has denied that wobble for six years.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: We put folded paper under it.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Her idea.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Good idea, honestly.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Then the roof made a sound like thunder eating gravel.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: I called her name.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: The chud called me a turnip.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: That means she was scared.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Usually that fungus says “moldy turnip.”

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Plain turnip is serious.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: I remember reaching for her.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: I remember the green necklace my chud always wears.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Then I remember dirt.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Wet dirt. New dirt.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: The sky looked wrong.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: The hills looked worse.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Our chimney landed over there.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: The neighbor’s fence landed over here.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: The neighbor has not stopped mentioning it.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Fair, I suppose.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: I dug at the front door.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: The frame shifted when I touched it.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: I stopped. I am irritating, not stupid.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: My chud would dispute both parts.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: She knows houses better than I do.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: She fixed the pantry shelf herself.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: I offered help.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: The fungus asked me to stand farther away.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: It has held for four years.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: The shelf, I mean.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: I hope the room around it held too.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: The chud keeps tea behind the blue tin.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Emergency money under the flour.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Spare key inside the ugly planter.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: The fungus says the planter is rustic.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: It is shaped like a screaming Bellsprout.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: I bought it for her.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: That is not the point.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: The point is my chud cannot be gone.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: We still have not settled the spoon question.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: And I called her a fungus. Which she was being.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Quietly. Mostly quietly.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: The chud called me worse.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Better, too. She is creative.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: I should have grabbed my chud instead of the table.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: I knew the table was unreliable.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: I knew she was right there.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: I keep thinking she yelled after I landed.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Or maybe that was somebody else.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: I cannot move the front wall safely.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: There may be a gap around the side.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: You look less likely to collapse it than I am.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: If the chud insults you, that means she is fine.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: Please check on my chud wife.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Check the crushed house for Lena. Look for a safe opening rather than breaking the front wall.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: She is alive. She is furious. Beautiful day.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: She is alive. She is furious. Beautiful day.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: It is a historic dispute now.

nodes.speaker: hank
nodes.text: See? Completely recovered.

nodes.speaker: lena
nodes.text: Hello? If that is Hank, the spoon drawer is still wrong.

nodes.speaker: lena
nodes.text: Oh. You are not Hank.

nodes.speaker: lena
nodes.text: Good. You look useful.

nodes.speaker: lena
nodes.text: The beam missed me. The cupboard did not.

nodes.speaker: lena
nodes.text: I am bruised, trapped, and extremely alive.

nodes.speaker: lena
nodes.text: Did he make you listen to the whole hundred?

nodes.speaker: lena
nodes.text: Of course he did.

nodes.speaker: lena
nodes.text: That man panics in paragraphs.

nodes.speaker: lena
nodes.text: He called me his chud wife, did he not?

nodes.speaker: lena
nodes.text: Tell him this fungus heard everything.

nodes.speaker: lena
nodes.text: Help me past this beam, then take this.

nodes.speaker: lena
nodes.text: You earned it long before you opened the door.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Lena is already safe outside. She offers you the matching Pallet charm kept with the rescued belongings.

nodes.speaker: lena
nodes.text: He told a stranger about the spoon drawer.

nodes.speaker: lena
nodes.text: Put one spoon wrong and I will bury you in the new dirt.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The safe opening is still hidden behind the crushed side of the house.

conversations.starter_gate: The owner's priority zero (2026-10-05): Oak gives the starter. modpack/config/cobblemon/starters.json sets allowStarterOnJoin false, so a new player joins starter-locked (Cobblemon 1.8.0 PlayerDataJsonBackend: starterLocked = !allowStarterOnJoin) and the native screen refuses them until Oak's oak_offer_choose runs `openstarterscreen` for them (tools/compile_dialogue.py open_starter_screen). That command unlocks, opens the config's five-way screen, and returns 0 without opening for a player who has already chosen; chooseStarter refuses a second pick (docs/research/notes/starter-selection.md section 5). oak_001 onward, and so record_oak_sendoff, is reached only by a player Cobblemon says has chosen: the starter_chosen entry rule, or the open action's own 0 result.
conversations.mode_choice: The owner, 2026-10-06: 'Oak offering the mode choice -- the difference explained without the words easy and hard. Codex wrote his dialogue. Build it.' Codex's lines are docs/story/CHALLENGE_GYM_DESIGN.md 'Oak's world-wide choice', written for ONE choice for the whole world; the choice is built PER PLAYER (docs/research/RCT_PER_PLAYER_MODE.md: rctmod's series is per player), so the three lines that said 'this campaign', 'this world' and 'everyone uses it' say 'your journey' and 'yours alone' here, and nothing else is changed. Standard = Normal, Full-Team = Challenge (docs/mechanics/OAK_AND_CHALLENGE.md). The choice sits between the starter and the send-off, and is written once (data/quests.json record_trainer_mode_*). Full-Team is not offered to a player who already holds the Boulder Badge: the series command would wipe their rctmod progress.

nodes.speaker: professor_oak
nodes.text: There you are. Nobody walks out of Pallet without a partner, and you will not be the first.

nodes.speaker: professor_oak
nodes.text: Eight are waiting in the lab. Choose one, and look after it. You only get the one.

nodes.speaker: professor_oak
nodes.text: Before I send you out, I need to write down which League rules you'll battle under.

nodes.speaker: professor_oak
nodes.text: Under Standard rules, Gym Leaders bring focused teams with a clear plan. Held items help, but not every Pokémon carries one.

nodes.speaker: professor_oak
nodes.text: Under Full-Team rules, every Gym Leader brings six that cover for each other, and their held items matter. Expect to need more than one counter.

nodes.speaker: professor_oak
nodes.text: The level limits are the same either way. Only the battles change.

nodes.speaker: professor_oak
nodes.text: This is for you alone, and once I write it down it stays. Which rules?

nodes.speaker: professor_oak
nodes.text: Standard rules, then? Once it's written, it stays.

nodes.speaker: professor_oak
nodes.text: Full-Team rules, then? Once it's written, it stays.

nodes.speaker: professor_oak
nodes.text: Your League rules are recorded: Standard rules.

nodes.speaker: professor_oak
nodes.text: Your League rules are recorded: Full-Team rules.

nodes.speaker: professor_oak
nodes.text: Your partner is ready. Route 1 begins north of town, just beyond the last houses.

nodes.speaker: professor_oak
nodes.text: Follow it toward Viridian. Keep the coast on your left and you cannot miss it.

nodes.speaker: professor_oak
nodes.text: Come back if the field guide raises questions. A map is useful only while the land agrees with it.

nodes.speaker: professor_oak
nodes.text: One more page for the field guide: birds nest in the great trees. Stand under a big crown and look up. Some kinds nest nowhere else.
nodes.placeholder: Claude, 2026-10-08 (unit WAY, the owner: 'the sapling hint ... An NPC mentioning birds nesting is enough'): a functional hint for Codex to replace. Said once, after the send-off, so every player who leaves Pallet hears it

nodes.text: Break it and it is yours again, so carry it with you when you move on. There is only the one.

nodes.text: Keep it in your pack. If you lose it, the Pallet Mart will sell you another, but I have only the one to give.

nodes.speaker: professor_oak
nodes.text: North through the houses, then Route 1. That road has been there longer than either of us.

nodes.speaker: professor_oak
nodes.text: There is no road to Viridian? Show me where your map stops matching the ground.

nodes.speaker: professor_oak
nodes.text: No. This is not an old map. The coastline, the river, even the distant ridge are wrong.

nodes.speaker: professor_oak
nodes.text: Pallet is here. I know these streets and these buildings. But the land outside town is not Kanto.

nodes.speaker: professor_oak
nodes.text: Follow the trail that actually exists. Someone beyond Pallet may have seen what happened from the outside.

nodes.speaker: professor_oak
nodes.text: Find someone who was outside Pallet when it happened, and bring me what they saw.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: One of the eight Professor Oak keeps in the lab. Talk to him to choose your partner.

nodes.speaker: mina
nodes.text: Oak is looking for you. Talk to him before you leave town.

nodes.speaker: mina
nodes.text: Route 1 used to begin here. I walked it enough times to know every bend.

nodes.speaker: mina
nodes.text: Now the Pallet road stops and a narrow trail keeps going through fields I have never seen.

nodes.speaker: mina
nodes.text: Some people say earthquake. Some say a storm. Storms do not replace the horizon.

nodes.speaker: mina
nodes.text: Look where the packed town soil meets the field. No shoulder, no drainage, no years of wear. Just a join.

nodes.speaker: mina
nodes.text: Tell Oak his map is not the problem. The place around it is.

nodes.speaker: mina
nodes.text: The old road is gone. Whatever happened, Pallet did not land cleanly.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: Oak is comparing maps. I am waiting until he says which one he trusts.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: My map agrees with Oak's. That only proves both maps remember the same world.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: Someone from my family was outside Pallet when this happened. If the town moved, they did not move with it.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: I will take the coast. You take the north trail.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: Find someone who watched Pallet arrive. Someone who was outside it, not asleep in it like us.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: North trail for you. Coast for me. We compare witnesses when we meet again.

nodes.speaker: brock
nodes.text: Talk to Professor Oak and Maren in Pallet first. They have the first half of this. Or earn the Boulder Badge from me, and I will tell you anyway.

nodes.speaker: brock
nodes.text: You came from the town in Pallet Meadows. I watched it arrive.

nodes.speaker: brock
nodes.text: The western horizon folded. For a moment the ground looked doubled, like two places were trying to occupy it.

nodes.speaker: brock
nodes.text: When our crews reached the meadow, Pallet stood where a native settlement had been.

nodes.speaker: brock
nodes.text: Homes, gardens, and the people living there were gone. Your town did not arrive on empty land.

nodes.speaker: brock
nodes.text: I do not blame Pallet. You look stranded, not victorious.

nodes.speaker: brock
nodes.text: But I will not call it random. We have found straight seams, displaced stone, and roads aligned to places that no longer exist.

nodes.speaker: brock
nodes.text: At the Pallet boundary, native plateau shale presses directly against Pallet soil, with no layer between them.

nodes.speaker: brock
nodes.text: So Pallet is not the only one. The rock does not say who did it.

nodes.speaker: brock
nodes.text: Show the local trainers you can handle the road ahead, then face me.

nodes.speaker: brock
nodes.text: If you earn the badge, go to Misty's lake town. Her people keep records of unusual arrivals and move aid through Lake Viltri.

nodes.speaker: brock
nodes.text: Two grounds joined with nothing between them. And a settlement gone to make room.

nodes.speaker: relief clerk
nodes.text: The lake office is still sorting arrivals. Bring the Boulder Badge from Brock, or his account of Pallet's arrival from Viltri Plateau, and I will open the ledger.

nodes.speaker: relief clerk
nodes.text: The families in this ledger did not travel here. Their streets folded under white light, and they woke beside Lake Viltri.

nodes.speaker: relief clerk
nodes.text: They arrived with medicine, work bags, children's toys, and Pokémon still guarding doorways that no longer existed.

nodes.speaker: relief clerk
nodes.text: The Haven Compact pulled them out of worlds that were already falling apart. Say what you like about the Compact, these people are alive.

nodes.speaker: relief clerk
nodes.text: Pallet's arrival carries the same pulse in our lake instruments, only cleaner and much larger.

nodes.speaker: relief clerk
nodes.text: That does not mean the Compact moved Pallet. And it says nothing about what disappeared at either end.

nodes.speaker: relief clerk
nodes.text: Misty compared our file with a reading relayed from Surge's town. The timing matches closely enough that he needs to see the original.

nodes.speaker: relief clerk
nodes.text: When the lake challenge is settled, take the sealed copy north. Surge's array can tell us whether this was weather or a controlled signal.

nodes.speaker: relief clerk
nodes.text: The rescues were real. What each one pushed out, nobody has asked yet.

nodes.text: I cannot compare an unlogged sample. Bring the Cascade Badge from Misty, or the relief clerk's file from the Lake Viltri office.

nodes.speaker: signal technician
nodes.text: The shoulder array recorded Pallet's pulse as a train of bursts, not a single impact.

nodes.speaker: signal technician
nodes.text: Each burst changed bearing by a measured amount. Natural noise does not correct its own direction.

nodes.speaker: signal technician
nodes.text: The spacing changes too: fire, wait, correct, fire again. Someone was steering the exchange while it happened.

nodes.speaker: signal technician
nodes.text: A team tried to remove these records before we finished the comparison. They withdrew when the town noticed them.

nodes.speaker: signal technician
nodes.text: The recovered pages match Misty's lake file and Brock's timestamp. Pallet was part of the same controlled system.

nodes.speaker: signal technician
nodes.text: Weapon or rescue line? Could be both. The record does not say.

nodes.speaker: signal technician
nodes.text: Next source is east of the massif, toward Peak Pond Hollow. Older signal, buried under altered ground.

nodes.speaker: signal technician
nodes.text: Repeated timing, corrected bearing, controlled bursts. Someone steered the exchange.

nodes.speaker: survey archivist
nodes.text: The survey ledger is sealed until the signal comparison from Mt Vessu arrives. Bring the Thunder Badge from Surge, or his signal technician's comparison.

nodes.speaker: survey archivist
nodes.text: This ledger is older than the exchange. Its stakes show the channel descending from the western tarn toward Peak Pond.

nodes.speaker: survey archivist
nodes.text: Walk the channel now and it rises twenty-two to twenty-nine blocks toward its recorded head. Water could never have carved the course we see.

nodes.speaker: survey archivist
nodes.text: The paper and the land cannot both describe the same terrain. The paper is dated, witnessed, and repeated across three surveys.

nodes.speaker: survey archivist
nodes.text: The western summit entry matters more. It lists homes, roads, gardens, and a full settled district where the Scar now stands.

nodes.speaker: survey archivist
nodes.text: That settlement did not erode. Its occupied volume was exchanged for the place that arrived here.

nodes.speaker: survey archivist
nodes.text: Pallet did not simply appear on new ground. Every transfer puts one place where another place was.

nodes.speaker: survey archivist
nodes.text: Some Compact workers want all forced transfers stopped. Others believe careful measurements can still save communities without repeating this loss.

nodes.speaker: survey archivist
nodes.text: The ledger shows the cost is real. Whether anyone can count every life at a destination, it cannot say.

nodes.speaker: survey archivist
nodes.text: Equipment and concealed crews have moved south toward Glacier Foot Fields. Koga has been tracking what they leave behind.

nodes.speaker: survey archivist
nodes.text: The old survey slopes down. The channel on the ground slopes up. A settled summit was exchanged.

nodes.speaker: marsh tracker
nodes.text: The marsh marks mean little without the Peak Pond survey. Bring the Rainbow Badge from Erika, or her survey archivist's record, south.

nodes.speaker: marsh tracker
nodes.text: The first anchor sites were neat circles. Each later site drifted farther from its own destination marks.

nodes.speaker: marsh tracker
nodes.text: Now reeds bend and Pokémon panic well beyond the equipment. The effect remains after the crews leave.

nodes.speaker: marsh tracker
nodes.text: These are not accidents. Every forced exchange leaves the next edge wider and sloppier.

nodes.speaker: marsh tracker
nodes.text: One recovered control plate carries the same ring symbol and a name: Hoopa.

nodes.speaker: marsh tracker
nodes.text: The frightened Pokémon gather before an activation and scatter afterward. Whatever carries the exchange is alive and unwilling.

nodes.speaker: marsh tracker
nodes.text: I do not think the Rift is natural. I think it is every forced use, piled up.

nodes.speaker: marsh tracker
nodes.text: Sabrina's town has the glacier, lake, signal, and memory reports. She can lay them side by side. I see one marsh.

nodes.speaker: marsh tracker
nodes.text: The anchors drift farther each time, and the living thing behind them is called Hoopa.

nodes.speaker: marsh tracker
nodes.text: Megas fight over the south end of the Rift, behind the Victory Road gate, and that gate wants eight badges. Before then, with Sabrina's badge, the Cutters' Gulch lookout on the Rift's east rim, about 2,300 blocks south of here, lets you down to the mine where their stones are cut.

nodes.speaker: Sabrina
nodes.text: The reports do not form a pattern until Koga's anchor record joins them. Bring the Soul Badge from Koga, or his marsh tracker's record.

nodes.speaker: Sabrina
nodes.text: The water records, glacier fractures, memory gaps, Pokémon behavior, and signal peaks all rise around the same exchanges.

nodes.speaker: Sabrina
nodes.text: They are separate measurements of one forced event, not five unrelated disasters.

nodes.speaker: Sabrina
nodes.text: When I reach for the mind at the center, I do not receive words. I receive fear before activation.

nodes.speaker: Sabrina
nodes.text: During the steering there is pain. Afterward there is confusion, as if the world has changed faster than Hoopa can understand it.

nodes.speaker: Sabrina
nodes.text: A large Compact community is running out of time. Without relocation, people will die when their world fails.

nodes.speaker: Sabrina
nodes.text: Another forced use may save them. It may also break Hoopa, widen the Rift, and exchange another occupied place.

nodes.speaker: Sabrina
nodes.text: So I cannot call them cruel. And I cannot call what they do harmless.

nodes.speaker: Sabrina
nodes.text: The preparations point south toward a major energy source at the Craters. Cross Tilpey's outflow and find what destination they chose.

nodes.speaker: Sabrina
nodes.text: Hoopa feels fear before the exchange, pain during it, and confusion after. The next activation is already being prepared.

nodes.text: The destination model means nothing without Sabrina's convergence record. Bring the Marsh Badge from Sabrina, or her record from the Tilpey north shore.

nodes.speaker: crater analyst
nodes.text: The Craters can power the Compact's next mass exchange. That is not what stopped us cold.

nodes.speaker: crater analyst
nodes.text: This destination model contains roads, occupied homes, active heat, and moving life at the selected coordinates.

nodes.speaker: crater analyst
nodes.text: Our warning was received. The attached acknowledgment orders the activation to proceed anyway.

nodes.speaker: crater analyst
nodes.text: Leadership no longer claims the destination is empty or that displacement can be avoided.

nodes.speaker: crater analyst
nodes.text: They chose their own endangered community over the people already living there.

nodes.speaker: crater analyst
nodes.text: Shutting down the crater stops this activation. The refugees are still waiting, and still not safe.

nodes.text: The southern watch has no reason to open its Rift file before the crater evidence arrives. Bring the Volcano Badge from Blaine, or his crater analyst's findings.

nodes.speaker: southern watch officer
nodes.text: We watched the crater crews retreat west with equipment they did not destroy.

nodes.speaker: southern watch officer
nodes.text: A message from Compact dissenters confirms the loyalists intend one final mass transfer through the Rift.

nodes.speaker: southern watch officer
nodes.text: The dissenters refuse to trade another population for their own. They gave us the operation's route and shutdown approach.

nodes.speaker: southern watch officer
nodes.text: They did not give us a way to save everyone. The refugees still face a collapsing world if the transfer ends.

nodes.speaker: southern watch officer
nodes.text: Giovanni kept this gym closed while the southern settlements prepared for another disappearance.

nodes.speaker: southern watch officer
nodes.text: His gym is the last test before the Rift road. He will not make it easy.

nodes.text: After the badge, follow the Rift's south-west arm to its fork, then the trunk toward the head. The final operation lies above the containment cradle.

nodes.speaker: southern watch officer

nodes.text: Victory Road is the Rift itself. The straight scars and displaced material are records left in the ground.

nodes.speaker: Rift surveyor
nodes.text: The effects worsen from the south-west arm to the fork, then along the trunk toward the head.

nodes.speaker: Rift surveyor
nodes.text: The Compact has begun its final activation above the containment cradle.

nodes.speaker: Rift surveyor
nodes.text: If it succeeds, their remaining community may survive by displacing another population and forcing Hoopa through one more exchange.

nodes.speaker: Rift surveyor
nodes.text: Stop it, and the refugees are still stranded. That does not make the method right.

nodes.speaker: Rift surveyor
nodes.text: Reach the cradle, end the forced steering, and release Hoopa. The League will not open while the activation remains live.

nodes.speaker: Rift surveyor
nodes.text: Nothing resets when this ends. Pallet, the missing settlement and the refugees will all still be here.

nodes.speaker: Rift surveyor
nodes.text: The road is the Rift floor: down the south-west arm to the fork, then up the trunk to the Deep, the great sink at its head. The Sink Gate stair on its south-east lip takes you down to the city's top ring.

nodes.speaker: League steward
nodes.text: The steering mechanism is silent. Hoopa is free, and the immediate widening of the Rift has stopped.

nodes.speaker: League steward
nodes.text: Nothing has snapped back. Pallet remains here, and the native settlement it replaced remains missing.

nodes.speaker: League steward
nodes.text: The rescued families still need homes. The dissenters still answer for the rescues, and for what the rescues displaced.

nodes.speaker: League steward
nodes.text: Nobody here will promise to undo it until someone knows how. Until then, we look after the people it stranded.

nodes.speaker: League steward
nodes.text: The League opening is not another emergency. This one is for you.

nodes.speaker: League steward
nodes.text: The trainers ahead will test the team that crossed the continent with you. Beat the Champion and this part is over. The repair goes on after.

nodes.speaker: League steward

nodes.speaker: digger
nodes.text: Mind the rail. It does not go anywhere anymore.

nodes.speaker: digger
nodes.text: This was the deepest cut the camp ever made.

nodes.speaker: digger
nodes.text: We followed a seam east. The rock got warmer every week.

nodes.speaker: digger
nodes.text: Nobody liked that. Nobody stopped digging, either.

nodes.speaker: digger
nodes.text: Then the props started creaking. Timber complains before it quits.

nodes.speaker: digger
nodes.text: Everyone else ran. Sensible people.

nodes.speaker: digger
nodes.text: I stayed to count the tools. Somebody has to.

nodes.speaker: digger
nodes.text: The roof came down behind them, not on them. I checked twice.

nodes.speaker: digger
nodes.text: Whatever we were cutting toward is under that heap now. Leave it there.

nodes.speaker: digger
nodes.text: Here. A cap from the pay tin, and amber out of the spoil.

nodes.speaker: digger
nodes.text: The camp will ask who has that amber. Tell them I said you could.

nodes.speaker: digger

nodes.text: Keep to the lee of the tower. The mouth wind comes sideways today.

nodes.speaker: keeper
nodes.text: Take the inland path past the light. The low outcrop where dark rock bands its foot carries Water Stone.

nodes.speaker: keeper
nodes.text: Use an iron pick. Dig down to the band and stop; the ore ends there. Leave the face ten minutes and the rock mends, but any chest you leave stays put.

nodes.speaker: keeper
nodes.text: Past the light, on the inland rise. Dark band at the foot; iron pick; stop at the band.

nodes.speaker: picker
nodes.text: Mind the young rows. They bruise before they bend.

nodes.speaker: picker
nodes.text: Past the upper tea rows, where old stone breaks the meadow, one face gives Leaf Stone and the brighter face gives Shiny Stone. A band of different rock runs along the foot of each.

nodes.speaker: picker
nodes.text: Use an iron pick. Dig down to the band and stop; the ore ends there. Give it ten quiet minutes and the rock mends, but any chest you leave stays put.

nodes.speaker: picker
nodes.text: Those giant old trees on the plateau are not empty, you know. Taillow nest all up the one west of the rows, and Spearow in the one off to the north-west. Walk in under the branches and they come down to look at you.

nodes.speaker: picker
nodes.text: Upper rows, old stone in the meadow: Leaf in the green face, Shiny in the bright one.

nodes.speaker: scavenger
nodes.text: Watch your step. Half these walls are ankle-high for a reason.

nodes.speaker: scavenger
nodes.text: Past the old square, look for the ruined house lot where terracotta rises in a low outcrop. The odd band along its foot carries Sun Stone.

nodes.speaker: scavenger
nodes.text: Use an iron pick. Dig down to the band and stop; the ore ends there. Leave it ten minutes and the rock mends, but any chest you leave stays put.

nodes.speaker: scavenger
nodes.text: Old square, ruined house lot, terracotta face. The Sun Stone ends at the band.

nodes.speaker: mason
nodes.text: Lanterns mark the streets. Past the last one, the wall is working ground.

nodes.speaker: mason
nodes.text: Along the south gallery, the pale dripstone face gives Moon Stone. The dark face near the Magnemite gives Thunder Stone. Each starts at a different band along the wall's foot.

nodes.speaker: mason
nodes.text: Use an iron pick. Dig down to the band and stop; the ore ends there. Leave it ten minutes and the rock mends, but any chest you leave stays put.

nodes.speaker: mason
nodes.text: South gallery: pale for Moon, dark by the Magnemite for Thunder. Stop at the foot band.

nodes.speaker: field_hand
nodes.text: If the mast starts humming, get indoors. If it only whistles, you are fine.

nodes.speaker: field_hand
nodes.text: Beside the weather mast, where the station cut breaks the square, a darker band runs along the outcrop's foot. That is the Ice Stone face.

nodes.speaker: field_hand
nodes.text: Use an iron pick. Dig down to the band and stop; the ore ends there. Leave it ten minutes and the rock mends, but any chest you leave stays put.

nodes.speaker: field_hand
nodes.text: And the giant pines out past the fields have birds nesting in them. Hoothoot in the one to the south, Starly in the one to the north-west, little Rowlet in the north-east one. Stand in under the branches and they show themselves.

nodes.speaker: field_hand
nodes.text: Weather mast, square-side cut. Dark band at the foot; stop when you reach it.

nodes.speaker: elder
nodes.text: The gorge carries every loose word downstream, so keep yours useful.

nodes.speaker: elder
nodes.text: At the bridgeward edge of the square, the outcrop splits two ways: Dusk Stone in the dark west face, Dawn Stone in the pale east face. Both begin at the band along the foot.

nodes.speaker: elder
nodes.text: Use an iron pick. Dig down to the band and stop; the ore ends there. Leave it ten minutes and the rock mends, but any chest you leave stays put.

nodes.speaker: elder
nodes.text: Bridgeward edge: dark west for Dusk, pale east for Dawn. No deeper than the band.

nodes.speaker: foreman
nodes.text: Helmet if you go past the yard. Pride will not stop falling stone.

nodes.speaker: foreman
nodes.text: Fire Stone shows in the plaza cut beside the Assayer, where hot rock bands the foot. The Thunder Stone is deeper, past the main workings where the dark seam starts to spark.

nodes.speaker: foreman
nodes.text: Use an iron pick. Dig down to the band and stop; the ore ends there. Leave it ten minutes and the rock mends, but any chest you leave stays put.

nodes.speaker: foreman
nodes.text: The Assayer on the plaza sells all ten kinds at a price. She buys none back.

nodes.speaker: foreman
nodes.text: Fire by the plaza, Thunder deep in the workings. Iron pick, and stop at the band.

nodes.speaker: hollis
nodes.text: Easy. Voices carry in there, and she's a light sleeper for something that size.

nodes.speaker: hollis
nodes.text: Ursaluna. Came over the ridge two winters back, dug herself in, and hasn't left. Highwire's been very polite about it.

nodes.speaker: hollis
nodes.text: No, your eyes are fine. She's bigger than the books say. Whatever she found to eat up here, it agreed with her.

nodes.speaker: hollis
nodes.text: Old folk say an Ursaring fed peat under a full moon wakes up as one of those. I've handled a lot of peat. Nobody's woken up as anything.

nodes.speaker: hollis
nodes.text: The little ones on the slope are Teddiursa. Hers, or they'd like to think so. She won't stir if you catch one. I'd ask first, though.

nodes.speaker: hollis
nodes.text: Go and look. Get close and she wakes, and she wakes cross. That's a fight, not a visit. Bring a team that can take it.

nodes.speaker: hollis
nodes.text: She sleeps and I watch. Wake her and you'd best be ready.

conversations.source: data/lopunny_house.json; docs: the owner's request of 2026-10-02 (data/lopunny_house.json request)

nodes.speaker: hopgood
nodes.text: Shut the door! SHUT it. They get out, and then they get cold, and then they get sad.

nodes.speaker: hopgood
nodes.text: Ellis Hopgood. Wipe your boots. You are standing on top of forty-one Buneary. Forty-two. There's a new one. She's shy.

nodes.speaker: hopgood
nodes.text: You know what a Lopunny is. Course you do. Tall. Poised. Ears like a pair of church spires. A Lopunny is what a Buneary is trying to be.

nodes.speaker: hopgood
nodes.text: Eleven years I've kept Buneary under this floor. Fed them, sung to them, knitted the little ones hats. Not one of them has ever turned into a Lopunny. Not ONE.

nodes.speaker: hopgood
nodes.text: Go on. Ask me why.

responses.text: Why not catch a wild Lopunny?

nodes.speaker: hopgood
nodes.text: Catch one? In a BALL? They're not luggage, they're family. They live free down there, in the warm, with the carrots.

nodes.speaker: hopgood
nodes.text: ...I'm told that's the problem. A Buneary comes into the world caring nothing for anybody. Zero, the professor's book says. Not low. Zero.

nodes.speaker: hopgood
nodes.text: It has to come to love its trainer, deep down, a hundred and sixty of whatever love is counted in. Then one day it grows a little, and up stands a Lopunny.

nodes.speaker: hopgood
nodes.text: Mine haven't got a trainer. Mine have got me. I've done the sums. I come to about nought.

nodes.speaker: hopgood
nodes.text: There ARE wild Lopunny on this isle. Out in the snow. I've seen them. They look at me the way you're looking at me now. Then they run.

nodes.speaker: hopgood
nodes.text: And it wouldn't be the same. I want to see one that grew up. One that was loved into it. You understand.

nodes.speaker: hopgood
nodes.text: So. You've got a trainer's face. Raise a Buneary. Love it until it can't stand it. And when it's a Lopunny, bring her here.

nodes.speaker: hopgood
nodes.text: Just so I can see one. Up close. In my house. I won't touch. Much.

nodes.speaker: hopgood
nodes.text: Well? Is she with you?

responses.text: How does a Buneary become a Lopunny, again?

nodes.speaker: hopgood
nodes.text: No? No. That's all right. That's all right. The kettle's on. It's always on.

nodes.speaker: hopgood
nodes.text: Oh. Oh, LOOK at her. Look at the EARS.

nodes.speaker: hopgood
nodes.text: The fluff. The posture. She's looking at me. Is she looking at me? She's looking at the door.

nodes.speaker: hopgood
nodes.text: You did that. Here. I bought this for them years ago: a Soothe Bell. The shop swore it would make them fond of me.

nodes.speaker: hopgood
nodes.text: They never noticed it. Maybe the next one of yours will. Mind the trapdoor on your way out.

nodes.speaker: hopgood
nodes.text: She was perfect. I've started a sketchbook. The Buneary are being very understanding about it.

nodes.speaker: wenna
nodes.text: Mind the rows. Half the trees are on the ground and the other half are full of Applin.

nodes.speaker: wenna
nodes.text: Marlow. We pressed cider here, my grandfather and my father and then me, until the storm took the roof and the last of the buyers took the ferry. I came over to see what was left.

nodes.speaker: wenna
nodes.text: That isn't a log at the end of the track. He came for the windfall the first autumn nobody picked it, and he's been eating his way up the rows ever since. Lies down where it lands.

nodes.speaker: wenna
nodes.text: Walk the last trees and you'll wake him. He doesn't get up for much, but he gets up for that, and he's not glad about it.

nodes.speaker: wenna
nodes.text: The apples that walk off are Applin. Always were. Father said a good year was one where the fruit stayed on the tree.

nodes.speaker: wenna
nodes.text: The press-house is behind me, roof half in. There's a cellar under the floor, trapdoor in the far corner. Father kept his best down there for a long winter, and I can't face the ladder. Whatever's in it does more good in your bag than in the damp.

nodes.speaker: wenna
nodes.text: Go on, the cellar. Mind the rubble on the way through, and let him sleep.

nodes.speaker: isaura
nodes.text: Sit if you like. Nothing happens for an hour, and then all of it happens at once.

nodes.speaker: isaura
nodes.text: Dray. Isaura Dray. The boatbuilders' guild kept this brow for the boats that went out to the Outer Sea, and I kept it for the guild. The guild moved to the mainland. The lamp didn't.

nodes.speaker: isaura
nodes.text: Every boat had an hour to be home by, and the hour was this: the sun in the gate. Stand at the benches and look west between the pillars. When the sun sits in it, everything that floats should be in sight of the pier. If you were still out, we rang.

nodes.speaker: isaura
nodes.text: The Evenfall was the last boat I rang for. Three masts, good oak, a crew of nineteen. She went out on a fair evening and the light went and she didn't come in. I rang till the sky was out.

nodes.speaker: isaura
nodes.text: The next dusk the Dreepy came up the slope. Pale, small, heads in the air. They drift up to the gate and look out to sea. The old hands say they're what the water gives back. I say they're waiting for the bell, same as I was.

nodes.speaker: isaura
nodes.text: They come when the light goes and only then. The sky turns the colour of the inside of a shell, and you have about a minute and a half before the dark takes them home. Sit on the benches. Don't walk at them.

nodes.speaker: isaura
nodes.text: Now and then something bigger comes up behind the small ones. Long, quiet, and it has opinions. I wouldn't be here with a party that's only just learned to win.

nodes.speaker: isaura
nodes.text: The guild left its lamp store in the hut, north-east corner, under the tarred sheet. Dusk Balls, mostly, and a tag some boatman swore by. Take it. I've no boats to light.

nodes.speaker: isaura
nodes.text: Go on. The evening's lighter than it looks. I'll keep the lamp.

conversations.source: data/dune_ruin.json; docs: the owner's request of 2026-10-02 (data/dune_ruin.json request)

nodes.speaker: varn
nodes.text: Mind the steps. The third one is sand all the way down. I just haven't told it yet.

nodes.speaker: varn
nodes.text: This was the Copperway Khan. Last stop on the freight road out of Fossick: ore south to the coast, salt and money back north.

nodes.speaker: varn
nodes.text: Copperajah pulled the wagons. When the road closed, the company turned them loose out here. Most went to dust. One didn't. You'll know him if you meet him.

nodes.speaker: varn
nodes.text: Three summers I've been pulling brass out of this hall. The rest of the place is under sand to the lintels, and nobody pays me to dig out a courtyard.

nodes.speaker: varn
nodes.text: Every khan kept a master's store, somewhere cool and down. The company ledger says this one was locked when the last caravan left. It doesn't say where the key went.

nodes.speaker: varn
nodes.text: That west wall was bricked up by somebody in a hurry. I'm not opening it. At night, something on the other side knocks back.

nodes.speaker: varn
nodes.text: Brass is brass. Whatever's behind that wall can stay there, as far as I'm concerned.

conversations.source: data/fossil_dig.json; docs: the owner's request of 2026-10-06 (data/fossil_dig.json request)

nodes.speaker: quarne
nodes.text: Mind where you put your boots. Everything down there is a great deal older than you are.

nodes.speaker: quarne
nodes.text: It's a bone bed. One dry season killed a whole herd on this mesa, and the clay kept them. We've cut it down a step at a time.

nodes.speaker: quarne
nodes.text: See the grey seams at the foot of the trench walls? That's where the fossils sit. Put a pick in one and you'll break it and get nothing.

nodes.speaker: quarne
nodes.text: Use a brush. Hold it on the seam and work it slow. If you haven't got one, make one from a feather, a copper ingot and a stick, or buy one at Cinderlee.

nodes.speaker: quarne
nodes.text: The wind silts a brushed seam back up in about a day. Come back and there'll be new grey in the walls. I've stopped asking how.

nodes.speaker: quarne
nodes.text: A fossil's only a stone until you wake it. For that you want the restoring machine: a Fossil Analyzer, a Restoration Tank and a Monitor, built together.

nodes.speaker: quarne
nodes.text: The Analyzer wants amethyst. Sableye and Glimmet shed it when you beat them. The Tank wants a Revive, and you'll be handed a few of those on the road.

nodes.speaker: quarne
nodes.text: Brush slow. Bring me anything with teeth and I'll try not to look jealous.

conversations.source: data/drovers_hollow.json; the owner's request of 2026-10-02 for places in the south (data/drovers_hollow.json request)

nodes.speaker: owen
nodes.text: Mind the fold gate. They'll walk straight out if you let them, and I'm past walking them back.

nodes.speaker: owen
nodes.text: Owen Cray. Last of the Hollow drovers. Forty winters we brought the herds down off the Rift's arms and wintered them in this barn.

nodes.speaker: owen
nodes.text: What's left is in the fold. Miltank for the milk, a few Tauros, Mudsdale for the hauling. They've been out here a long while, mind. They're not tame and they're not small.

nodes.speaker: owen
nodes.text: The Hollow's named for the spring at the back of the barn. Dry ravine, wet barn. My father swore the water came from somewhere older than us.

nodes.speaker: owen
nodes.text: When it ran low he dug behind the trough to chase it. Found an old working down there instead, and kept the best of each season's tack in it. Never told me what. Trapdoor behind the trough, if you want to look.

nodes.speaker: owen
nodes.text: And if you go east up the rise, give the big Bouffalant room. Hornwall, they call him. We never drove him. Nobody will.

nodes.speaker: owen
nodes.text: Behind the trough, down the ladder, along the old working. Shut the trapdoor after you, or the calves go exploring.

nodes.speaker: nia
nodes.text: The clinic is for people the Rift has already hurt. If the Compact sent you, you are early. Nobody comes down here without Giovanni's Earth Badge.

nodes.speaker: nia
nodes.text: You made it down into the Deep. Then you know the Compact has started the final steering cycle.

nodes.speaker: nia
nodes.text: I joined to carry people out of collapsing places. I still believe they deserve carrying.

nodes.speaker: nia
nodes.text: Elara's order would save them by choosing strangers to disappear. That is not rescue anymore.

nodes.speaker: nia
nodes.text: Brann holds the briefing hall. Oren is in anchor control, keeping the machine stable because an unstable stop could tear the Deep open.

nodes.speaker: nia
nodes.text: Show Oren this route packet. It contains Tomas's occupied-site reading and my authorization to evacuate the cradle staff.

nodes.speaker: nia
nodes.text: Get the anchors down safely. Then Elara has no operation left to defend.

nodes.speaker: nia
nodes.text: Headquarters is the black tower on the top ring, west side. Elara keeps its door herself. My packet gets you past her; it will not get you her blessing. Climb.

nodes.speaker: nia
nodes.text: Briefing hall, anchor control, then Elara. Do not open the shaft while the anchors are live.

nodes.speaker: nia

nodes.text: You should not be in this tower. Go back down before somebody less patient finds you.

nodes.speaker: brann
nodes.text: Nia sent you. I hoped she would choose evacuation over mutiny.

nodes.speaker: brann
nodes.text: Every person below us has watched a home fail. I will not call them villains for wanting one place that stays.

nodes.speaker: brann
nodes.text: But I read Tomas's result. The destination is occupied, and Elara ordered the cycle anyway.

nodes.speaker: brann
nodes.text: My people will not fight a trainer who came through eight leaders to stop that. I will.

nodes.speaker: brann
nodes.text: This hall is the last place I can still turn you round. Walk back down, or show me you can stop this without killing the city.

nodes.speaker: brann

nodes.speaker: oren
nodes.text: Do not touch the board. Not you, not anyone the Captain has not cleared.

nodes.speaker: oren
nodes.text: Do not touch the board yet. A dead anchor and a safe anchor are not the same thing.

nodes.speaker: oren
nodes.text: I kept telling myself careful work made the exchanges right. Smaller losses, one more family carried out.

nodes.speaker: oren
nodes.text: Tomas proved the target is occupied. There is no cleaner setting left.

nodes.speaker: oren
nodes.text: The three outer relays must go quiet before the core. Use the marked sequence; I will hold the return load.

nodes.speaker: oren
nodes.text: Outer relays first, then the core. My hand is on the return load.

nodes.speaker: oren
nodes.text: All four are down. The Rift is no longer being steered, but Hoopa is still bound in the cradle.

nodes.speaker: oren
nodes.text: Elara has the shaft interlock. Go down and show her the board is dark.

nodes.speaker: oren
nodes.text: Anchors are down. The secure shaft is still locked, and Elara holds the door above it.

nodes.speaker: oren

nodes.speaker: elara
nodes.text: Whoever you are, this door is not on your route.

nodes.speaker: elara
nodes.text: Jun let you into the Deep. That was his to give. This door is mine.

nodes.speaker: elara
nodes.text: Behind me is the operation that keeps every light down here burning. It has no use for a trainer without orders. Step back.

nodes.speaker: elara
nodes.text: Nia's packet. She thinks an evacuation order makes you staff.

nodes.speaker: elara
nodes.text: I have read Tomas's trace more times than she has. I know what is on the other side of the cycle.

nodes.speaker: elara
nodes.text: Go up, then. Captain Saye holds the briefing hall, and Oren will show you why the machine is still running.

nodes.speaker: elara
nodes.text: When you have run out of arguments, come back down. I will be here. The shaft under this floor answers to me.

nodes.speaker: elara
nodes.text: The anchors are still live. Nothing you say to me changes while the machine is running.

nodes.speaker: elara
nodes.text: Listen to the city before you call this simple. Every light below us belongs to someone the Compact carried out.

nodes.speaker: elara
nodes.text: We found them air, medicine, years. The ordinary world did not arrive to help.

nodes.speaker: elara
nodes.text: I knew the destination was occupied. I ordered the cycle because I could name the people who would die if I stopped.

nodes.speaker: elara
nodes.text: I never once asked for the other names.

nodes.speaker: elara
nodes.text: The interlock answers to me. If you want the shaft, you will have to take it from the one who ordered the cycle.

nodes.speaker: elara
nodes.text: Not with that team. One of yours is past what your badges let you command. Put it in the PC and come back.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: Welcome to Shrew Station. Mind the copper, it's new. We study the things the old stories say live in this region: the legends, and the places they keep coming back to.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: Imogen Vale, Director. Out on the platform is the Eon shrine: one altar for Latias, one for Latios, built over the deepest water we could reach.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: Fair warning, because the last visitor wanted a promise. We have never seen an altar answer. Not that one, not any. Until we do, nothing that might wake one leaves this station.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: What can the station do for you?

responses.text: Why build a shrine on the water?
Could I have a feather? Or a crown?
I stood on the thunder tower in a storm.
I went inside the fire tower in the Craters.
My Kubfu is nearly grown. Do you know of the scrolls?
My Kubfu is growing. Do you know of the scrolls?
I raised a Type: Null. Do you know of the memories?
I'm raising a Type: Null. Do you know of the memories?

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: Know of them? We keep two. A Kubfu does not grow into its last shape by training alone: it reads one of two scrolls, and the scroll decides how it fights for the rest of its life.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: Darkness makes a single, crushing strike. Waters makes a flowing run of blows. The station gives one, once, to whoever raised the Kubfu. Not both. You choose.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: Which will your Kubfu read?

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: Darkness, then. Here: the Scroll of Darkness, from our store. Hold it out to your Kubfu once it reaches level 45, and not before.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: Write and tell me what it becomes. The station has only ever read about it.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: Waters, then. Here: the Scroll of Waters, from our store. Hold it out to your Kubfu once it reaches level 45, and not before.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: Write and tell me what it becomes. The station has only ever read about it.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: We keep two, and one of them is yours when your Kubfu is ready for it. Come back with the Soul Badge: a Kubfu that has not seen that much will not read either.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: Know of them? We keep all seventeen. Type: Null was built to carry one, and the mask holds it back. Once it grows into Silvally, the disc it holds decides its type.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: The station gives the whole set, once, to whoever raised it. One disc would fix it to one type, and changing is the point. Will you take them?

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: Here: seventeen memories, from our store. Give your Silvally one to hold, and change it whenever the fight calls for another. Type: Null becomes Silvally at level 45.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: Write and tell me which one it settles on. The station has only ever read about them.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: We keep a set for it, and it is yours when your Type: Null is ready for it. Come back with the Soul Badge: before then a memory would only sit in your bag.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: Three things. The sea past the platforms, where the shelf drops away into water nobody has sounded to the bottom. The towers on the coasts and the summits: there's one up this very shore. And the items nobody makes.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: Every altar we know of wants something held up to it: a feather, a crown, a dew. Not one of them is sold, crafted or found anywhere we have looked. That is either an accident or a lock.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: I think it's a lock. We are trying to find the key without breaking the door.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: The old books say Latias and Latios guard a city built on canals. A shrine you can only reach by walking over water seemed the right kind of home for them.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: Mireille keeps it, out on the platform. Ask her about the dews. Ask her about the old one, too.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: Not yet. The rule is mine and it is simple: nothing leaves this station until someone shows me an altar answering. I won't hand out a key to a door that may be painted on the wall.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: When that day comes, my people will tell you what each one costs. Not money. Work: a storm watched, a parcel carried, a harvest brought in.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: You stood up there in the thunder and came down again. Then the station owes you this: a thunder feather, from our store.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: If the thunder tower's altar answers anyone, it should answer that. Go with every badge you have.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: Up the crater's flank, past Blaine's town, for a feather. Here: an ember feather, from our store. Mind your sleeves.

nodes.speaker: vale
nodes.text: The fire tower's altar is its own business. We have only ever read about it answering.

nodes.speaker: brandt
nodes.text: Brandt, field officer. I count clouds and time storms.

nodes.speaker: brandt
nodes.text: I also run the station's errands to the other camps. Frostpeak, mostly. Dr. Halvard watches the tower on the summit, and she keeps the best notes in the region.

nodes.speaker: brandt
nodes.text: Something you need?

nodes.speaker: brandt
nodes.text: Wind, cold, pressure, and the hour the thunder starts. No lightning rods out here: they pull every Electric type off the coast, and I like my instruments unchewed.

nodes.speaker: brandt
nodes.text: Not today. The Director has frozen every errand that ends in a feather until we have seen an altar answer. Caution, she calls it.

nodes.speaker: brandt
nodes.text: Good. This spyglass is calibrated against ours. Take it to Dr. Halvard at the Frostpeak camp, stand on her instrument deck and hold it out where she can see it.

nodes.speaker: brandt
nodes.text: She'll swap it for her season's notes. Bring those back in your hand, and the station's glacier feather is yours.

nodes.speaker: brandt
nodes.text: Halvard's handwriting. Three winters of frost on that tower, in one bundle. Thank you.

nodes.speaker: brandt
nodes.text: Here: the glacier feather. Articuno is said to come to it. Nobody here has seen it come.

nodes.speaker: quill
nodes.text: Shh. No, not you, the floor creaks. Tobias Quill, archivist. Everything the station knows is written down in this room, and most of it is questions.

nodes.speaker: quill
nodes.text: What can I find for you?

responses.text: Could I trade for the crown?

nodes.speaker: quill
nodes.text: Four exhibits we do not have. A glacier feather, a thunder feather, an ember feather, and a crown of roots. Every altar we know of wants one, and none is made anywhere we have found.

nodes.speaker: quill
nodes.text: The labels are all we have, so the cases stay empty. And the dews, for the Eon shrine: Mireille has opinions about the dews.

nodes.speaker: quill
nodes.text: Mew's fossil is the odd one out: there is a way to make it, if you can find the parts. But what answers that shrine is far stronger than any Pokemon a trainer here could hold. We do not encourage it.

nodes.speaker: quill
nodes.text: Not yet. The crown stays in its case until two things are true: an altar has been seen to answer, and the Director is satisfied that whoever wears it could hold what comes.

nodes.speaker: quill
nodes.text: Let me count them.

nodes.speaker: quill
nodes.text: Sixteen, I said. Shaderoot carrots, from the Crown Cemetery's own field. The crown's old keepers asked a full harvest, and we keep to their price.

nodes.speaker: quill
nodes.text: Sixteen shaderoot carrots from the cemetery's field. That was the price the crown's old keepers asked, and it is paid.

nodes.speaker: quill
nodes.text: The crown. Calyrex is said to come to it, and it is strong. You'll want every badge you have, and then some.

nodes.speaker: mireille
nodes.text: Careful on the dais. Mireille. I keep the shrine, which mostly means I keep the gulls off it.

nodes.speaker: mireille
nodes.text: Red for Latias, blue for Latios. Each altar wants a dew of its own colour, and the grey stone between them is where the old books say they come down.

nodes.speaker: mireille
nodes.text: Ask, if you like.

responses.text: Would they come to my ball?
I've met the three spirits of the lakes.

nodes.speaker: mireille
nodes.text: A ruby dew and a sapphire dew. Nobody here has ever made one or sold one. The ledger says they were given, once, to people the three lake spirits had met. We keep to the ledger.

nodes.speaker: mireille
nodes.text: Some would. The ledger has them young and old: some no stronger than a gym leader's best, and sometimes one so old that no trainer in this region could ever hold it.

nodes.speaker: mireille
nodes.text: If the old one comes, let it go home. That's my rule, not the ledger's.

nodes.speaker: mireille
nodes.text: Not yet. The Director keeps the dews locked in the ledger room until someone shows her an altar answering. I think she's right.

nodes.speaker: mireille
nodes.text: Mesprit, Azelf and Uxie. All three. Then the ledger says you are owed these, and I keep to the ledger.

nodes.speaker: mireille
nodes.text: A ruby dew and a sapphire dew. If these altars answer anyone, they'll answer you. And if the old one comes...

nodes.speaker: mireille
nodes.text: ...you know my rule.

nodes.speaker: tobiah
nodes.text: Mind the edge. There's no floor past the table. There used to be.

nodes.speaker: tobiah
nodes.text: Tobiah Rusk. This was a whole house once, nine paces by nine. You're standing in the five that stayed.

nodes.speaker: tobiah
nodes.text: Sit, if you like. That chair's free. It's always free.

responses.text: Who lived in the other half?

nodes.speaker: tobiah
nodes.text: One night the light went white. Not lightning. Lightning comes and goes. This came and stood there, along one line, about as long as it takes to say so.

nodes.speaker: tobiah
nodes.text: Then it stopped, and the house stopped at the table. Look at the boards. Not broken. Cut. Like a loaf.

nodes.speaker: tobiah
nodes.text: And the ground past the line isn't our ground. Ours had a well and a plum tree. That's somebody else's meadow. The line goes right on across it, both ways, as far as you care to walk.

nodes.speaker: tobiah
nodes.text: Nell. My wife. She was in the kitchen, and the kitchen was on that side.

nodes.speaker: tobiah
nodes.text: I don't believe she's dead. A cut that clean doesn't kill anybody. It moves them.

nodes.speaker: tobiah
nodes.text: So somewhere there's half a house with a kettle and a stove and no chairs, and Nell in it, cross with me for having the chairs.

nodes.speaker: tobiah
nodes.text: Where would I go? If she ever finds her way back, she'll come to the line. This is the line.

nodes.speaker: tobiah
nodes.text: I set her place every night. Cup on the table, chair pulled out.

nodes.speaker: tobiah
nodes.text: You get about, you trainers. If you ever come on half a house with a kettle in it and no chairs, would you tell her?

nodes.speaker: tobiah
nodes.text: Tell her I kept the chairs. She'll know what it means.

nodes.speaker: tobiah
nodes.text: Thank you. Her place is set. Mind the edge on your way out.

nodes.speaker: tobiah
nodes.text: No. Course not. Nobody could. Sit a minute anyway. The chair's free.

nodes.speaker: corran
nodes.text: Stand still. No, there. You're on my line.

nodes.speaker: corran
nodes.text: Corran Vey, Survey of the Meridian. I've chained this line four hundred miles, straight as a stretched string, a pole every eight paces.

nodes.speaker: corran
nodes.text: And then it walks into the sea. My chain says there's ground out there. The sea is of another opinion.

nodes.speaker: corran
nodes.text: Bearing thirty. Eight paces a pole. What is it?

nodes.speaker: corran
nodes.text: On my plan: a farm called Hollins, a ford, the Kestrel road. Out there: fish. I've rowed the bearing. Water to the mainland, and the mainland doesn't match my plan either.

nodes.speaker: corran
nodes.text: Lost? I am precisely located. It's the world that has wandered.

nodes.speaker: corran
nodes.text: Here is the trouble. My compass came with me, from wherever I was. Now it won't settle. It turns and turns, like it's looking for a north that isn't here.

nodes.speaker: corran
nodes.text: Bring me a new one. Four iron and a redstone, made here, from iron dug here. A compass made in a place knows where that place is. That one I'd trust.

nodes.speaker: corran
nodes.text: Give it here. Hold the lamp. Look at that. Steady as a church.

nodes.speaker: corran
nodes.text: It points that way. Not at anything I know. But it points the same way twice, and that is all a surveyor ever asks of anything.

nodes.speaker: corran
nodes.text: This is yours. My datum: the stone every measurement on this line was taken from. An Everstone. Nothing changes it. I set it in that block the morning I began.

nodes.speaker: corran
nodes.text: It never moved an inch. Everything round it did. I'll start a new line from here, off the new compass.

nodes.speaker: corran
nodes.text: New line, bearing thirty. First pole's in. Mind it on your way past.

nodes.speaker: nan
nodes.text: Not through the gate. They're jumpy enough as it is.

nodes.speaker: nan
nodes.text: That's the fold, and that's the flock. Nineteen ewes, and not one of them will cross that gap. They're waiting on the bell.

nodes.speaker: nan
nodes.text: Tolly. My Flaaffy. Bellwether eleven winters, and never once left them. Dawn today I found his strap slipped over the hook. Not torn. Slipped. He took it off himself.

nodes.speaker: nan
nodes.text: Nan looks past you, down the road.

nodes.speaker: nan
nodes.text: South. They all go south, come back-end: down the old drove road to the winter fold at the foot of the Tear. My brother Jory keeps it. But Tolly never goes straight. He rings the cairns first. Likes to be sure the way is marked.

nodes.speaker: nan
nodes.text: His bell cracked at spring shearing. Flat, with a rattle in it, like a pebble in a tin. Every other bell on this down sings. His doesn't. You'd know it in a gale.

nodes.speaker: nan
nodes.text: Then keep to the road and listen. If you reach the winter fold before I do, tell Jory the ewes are fine and the fool isn't.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: A hook on the gate post, worn bright. The loop is empty. The leather isn't cut or chewed: it was slid off over the post.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: Slid off over the post, exactly as Nan said. Whoever did this knew how a strap works.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: The ewe stands in the gap with her nose to the south and does not move. When you step closer she plants her feet.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: You flick the bell with a finger. A bright, clean note, and it carries over the down. Pretty. Not the one.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: A deep, round note, sweet as a well. Somebody's good bell, hung here for luck. Not the one.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: You flick it. Flat. A dull clack with a rattle under it, a pebble in a tin.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: Over the arm, looped twice, hangs a braided strap of blue yarn. Not cut. Slipped.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: Below the cairn, in the soft ground: a small cloven print, then another, going away south-east where the old drove wall runs down toward the glacier's foot. You take the strap.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: The cracked bell clacks in its own small way. The strap is already in your pack.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: WIND SSW, rising. Pond: skinning. Ewes: gone quiet. Tonight. Chalked fresh, in a hand that has chalked it every autumn evening of its life.

nodes.speaker: gorse
nodes.text: Shut the door, you're letting the weather in.

nodes.speaker: gorse
nodes.text: Not that I mind. It's all the same weather. Gorse. I've watched the Tear from here since before it had that name.

nodes.speaker: gorse
nodes.text: Every back-end it breathes out. Cold runs off the ice like rain off a roof, down the trough and onto the fields. First a draught at the ankles, then the ponds skin over, then the ewes go quiet. Tonight, I'd say.

nodes.speaker: gorse
nodes.text: Gorse doesn't look up from the board.

responses.text: Why is the winter fold where it is?
I found his strap at the cairns.
May I take from the commons box?

nodes.speaker: gorse
nodes.text: Behind the long swell of the field, out of the line of the trough. The cold runs past it, not through it. The ewes know that. Nobody told them.

nodes.speaker: gorse
nodes.text: Dawn, going south, bell clacking like a dropped spoon. Didn't stop for the stew. He'll be at the winter fold by dark if he has any sense. Flaaffy don't, as a rule, but he's an old one.

nodes.speaker: gorse
nodes.text: Blue yarn, slid clean. Then he went on ahead on purpose, to be at the fold when the front comes. Typical. Look for the turf roof in the open, south-east, past the shrine niche.

nodes.speaker: gorse
nodes.text: Walkers' box, under the bench. Take one parcel and leave the rest for the next. That's the rule, and the box is older than the rule.

nodes.speaker: gorse
nodes.text: Which?

nodes.speaker: gorse
nodes.text: A cloth parcel tied with heather. Inside, three tins of resin salve, the kind that takes the sting out of anything.

nodes.speaker: gorse
nodes.text: Two stoppered flasks of lamp oil and a twist of wicks, still warm from the shelf over the hearth.

nodes.speaker: gorse
nodes.text: Good. Now go on. The front doesn't wait on a conversation.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: A chalk tally on a board: nineteen strokes for the ewes in, and a ring beside them, left open, for the bell that's out.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: You hold up the blue strap. Tolly goes very still, then lowers his head and lets you slip it over. A spark jumps from his wool to your wrist. Round his neck, on a bit of cord, the cracked bell gives its flat little rattle.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: A Flaaffy with no strap and a cracked bell on a bit of cord, standing very straight on a flat stone as though he'd been posted there. He lets you come near. He doesn't let you touch him.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: Tolly keeps his post on the stone. The flock is down in the fold; the nearest ewes keep half an eye on him.

nodes.speaker: jory
nodes.text: Keep left of the wall. The ground's soft by the stone.

nodes.speaker: jory
nodes.text: Jory Tarrow. Winter fold. If Nan sent you with a message, it's 'hurry up', and I've heard it.

nodes.speaker: jory
nodes.text: Jory wipes his hands on his coat.

responses.text: Nan says the ewes are fine and the fool isn't.

nodes.speaker: jory
nodes.text: That's the third time she's sent me that. The fool's on his stone by the pen and has been since noon, ringing like a spoon in a pot. Go and tell him he's in trouble.

nodes.speaker: jory
nodes.text: On the flat stone by the pen, where else. Go and look. Then come and tell me you saw him, because Nan won't believe me.

nodes.speaker: jory
nodes.text: Turf holds heat and sheds wind, and the roof's the one thing the Tear can't read. Cut the same sods my father did. Same grass, probably.

nodes.speaker: jory
nodes.text: That's Tolly's strap round his neck. You went by the cairns? Then you did it properly.

nodes.speaker: jory
nodes.text: Take this. A lodestone the Tarrows have handed round the bellwethers since before my time: they all end up leaning on it. It'll do more good in your team than in my rafters. And these, for the road.

nodes.speaker: jory
nodes.text: You found him. That's more than the dog managed. He won't say where he's been; he never does.

nodes.speaker: jory
nodes.text: Here, for the road. And if you pass Nan again, tell her I said she was right, and she'll be unbearable all winter.

nodes.speaker: jory
nodes.text: Mind the front tonight. Gorse reckons it'll be a cold one, and Gorse is usually right.

nodes.speaker: bettany
nodes.text: Sit by the fire, if your legs still bend. Mine don't. Not up hills.

nodes.speaker: bettany
nodes.text: Bettany Oake. Forty years I panned these creeks. Gold, a bit. Hard stones. Once a sheet of something that had been a Steelix's hide, polished up like a kettle.

nodes.speaker: bettany
nodes.text: Well? You didn't walk all the way out here for my tea.

responses.text: Do you still have a claim?

nodes.speaker: bettany
nodes.text: Moved. One summer they ran where they'd always run. Next spring half of them came down the other side of the hill like they'd never heard of me.

nodes.speaker: bettany
nodes.text: A creek doesn't do that. Not in forty years, not in four hundred. But I'm an old woman with a pan, and nobody asked me.

nodes.speaker: bettany
nodes.text: Number Four. My best. Up where the old creek bed was, before it took itself off.

nodes.speaker: bettany
nodes.text: Walk into the sunset from here, uphill, till the ground stops rising. Couple of hundred paces. My cairn's on the top: three stones high, with my pick stood in it.

nodes.speaker: bettany
nodes.text: There's a barrel set in the ground at the foot of it. Whatever's in it, keep. I'd only sell it, and who'd I sell it to out here?

nodes.speaker: bettany
nodes.text: Did you. Is the pick still standing? Good. Leave it there. It's minding the place for me.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Sit down, sit down. Best seat on the plain. Look west. See the wall on the skyline, and the gate in it?

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Hale Brannock. Seven badges. Thirty-one years ago I walked up to that gate with my Golem and my Nidoking and old Burl, and came back down the same road.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Lovely evening for it. It's always a lovely evening for it.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: I meant to. Next spring, I said. Then my knees, then Burl's knees. You'd be surprised how many springs there are, and how quick they go.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: So I sit here instead, where I can see it. Seven on the board and a hole where the eighth goes. I don't mind the hole. It's honest.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Boulder, Cascade, Thunder, Rainbow, Soul, Marsh, Volcano. And the gap. I made that board the week I came back down. Thought I'd have it filled by the autumn.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: You've... let me see it. No, hold it up. To the light.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Well. There it is. That's what it looks like up close. I always wondered if it'd be heavier.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Here. These were Burl's Leftovers. My Snorlax. He held them through every fight we ever had, and the one we lost. They ought to go through that gate, and he can't take them.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Go on, then. You've been through it once. Go through it again for the both of us, on your way out to the League.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: The hole's still in the board. Funny. I find I don't mind it at all now.

nodes.text: Mind the chips. Hesketh Fell. I've the felling order for this wood, every birch in it, and I've felled every birch in it.

nodes.speaker: hesketh
nodes.text: Bar that one. An oak, in a birch wood, bang in the middle. Six weeks I've been at it. Three axes. Bounced, bounced, bent.

nodes.speaker: hesketh
nodes.text: It'll come down. They all come down in the end.

nodes.speaker: hesketh
nodes.text: Not a tree. Forty years I've been felling. Bark, branches, green on top. That's a tree.

nodes.speaker: hesketh
nodes.text: Mind you, it's never dropped a leaf. And some mornings it's a yard nearer my fire than it was. Roots settling. They do that.

nodes.speaker: hesketh
nodes.text: Go and give it a kick if you don't believe me. Mind your foot. Mind my tree.

nodes.speaker: hesketh
nodes.text: Watering it? It's a tree. It gets rained on.

nodes.speaker: hesketh

nodes.speaker: hesketh

nodes.speaker: agnes
nodes.text: Is someone there? Come round where I can hear you. Agnes Merrow. I'd offer you tea, but the kettle's the one thing in here I can't find any more.

nodes.speaker: agnes
nodes.text: My eyes went the winter before last. Not all at once. Things went soft at the edges, and then the edges went.

nodes.speaker: agnes
nodes.text: Sit if you like. The step's sound.

responses.text: How long have you lived here?
Is there anything I can do?
It says 'She said yes. I still can't believe it.'

nodes.speaker: agnes
nodes.text: Sixty-one years. Edwin built her the spring we married. The horse went long ago, and then Edwin did, and the wagon and I just stayed where we'd stopped.

nodes.speaker: agnes
nodes.text: There is, if you've young legs. Sixty paces north, up the rise, there's an old oak. Dead now, I'm told. The morning we married, Edwin carved our names in it.

nodes.speaker: agnes
nodes.text: Then he went round the back of the tree and carved something else, and came back laughing, and never would tell me what. 'You'll read it when you need to,' he said.

nodes.speaker: agnes
nodes.text: Well. I need to now, and I can't. Would you go and read it to me? Exactly as it's written, mind. I'll know if you're making it up.

nodes.speaker: agnes
nodes.text: That's the front, love. I know the front, I was there. Round the back. The side he wouldn't let me see.

nodes.speaker: agnes
nodes.text: Ha! He'd never have carved that. Not where people could read it.

nodes.speaker: agnes
nodes.text: ...Say it again.

nodes.speaker: agnes
nodes.text: 'She said yes. I still can't believe it.' Sixty-one years and he never told me that. The daft old thing.

nodes.speaker: agnes
nodes.text: Here. Hold out your hand. That's the stone he gave me that morning instead of a ring. Found it in the creek. Said it was warmer than gold. It still is.

nodes.speaker: agnes
nodes.text: A Sun Stone, the woman at the market called it, years after. You have it. I've got what the tree says now. That'll do me.

nodes.speaker: agnes
nodes.text: Sixty paces north. She said yes. I'd say it again.
