nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: HALT! Challenger approaching! You have entered... PIP'S GYM!

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: I'm Pip. I'm the leader. I haven't got any Pokemon yet, Mum says when I'm eleven, but I've got the gym and I'm practising the speeches.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Well? Are you challenging or not?

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: 'So! A challenger dares to enter my gym! My Pokemon are... going to be extremely strong! Prepare to battle for... the Twig Badge!'

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: ...The middle bit needs work. Erika does hers without even shouting. I don't know how you do a speech without shouting.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: How many have you got? Is Erika next? Erika's the best. She does flowers AND fighting. When you beat her you have to come and tell me everything.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: You BEAT ERIKA? ...Was she nice about it? I bet she was nice about it. Did her gym smell of flowers? I KNEW it.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: I'm going to have a flower bit in my gym. And tea. Hay tea. It's like tea but it's hay.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Invisible walls? Invisible WALLS? ...Right. I'm putting invisible walls in. You can't see them, so they might be in already.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Did she read your mind? Read mine. Go on. What am I thinking? ...Wrong. Lunch. I'm nearly always thinking about lunch.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: A QUIZ? At a GYM? ...Right. Question one: what is my name. Question two: what is my gym called. You'd win. That's the trouble with quizzes.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: ...All eight. ALL eight. Can I hold them? I won't drop them. I'll drop them. I won't.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Right. Stand on the line. 'Challenger! You have beaten every leader in the land, and now you have beaten... the leader of PIP'S GYM!'

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: You didn't have to fight me. That's the rule. I just made it. Here. The Twig Badge.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: It's not a twig, it's my shiniest stone. I was saving it to be the badge for when I had a real gym. You're the first one who's won it. Don't tell Erika it's better than hers.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Twig Badge winners: you. Everyone else: not yet. Come back when I'm eleven and I'll battle you properly.

nodes.text: ...ninety-eight, ninety-nine, A HUNDRED. Coming, ready or not! ...Oh. You're not Lettie.

nodes.speaker: tam
nodes.text: I'm Tam. We're playing hide and seek. I counted to a hundred. That was this morning. I've counted to a hundred eleven times.

nodes.speaker: tam
nodes.text: Have you seen my sister? She's got a red hat.

nodes.speaker: tam
nodes.text: Yes. No. Yes. It's not cheating if it's a grown-up. She always hides somewhere low. Or somewhere high. She's very good.

nodes.speaker: tam
nodes.text: Mum's calling us in for tea soon, and if we're not in for tea I'm in trouble, because I'm the oldest. By six minutes.

nodes.speaker: tam
nodes.text: Behind the trees. All the trees. Up the trees. Not under things. I don't like under things. She knows I don't like under things.

nodes.speaker: tam
nodes.text: In a BUSH? Up the bank? ...I walked past that bush eleven times.

nodes.speaker: tam
nodes.text: Did she say she won? She'll say she won. ...She won.

nodes.speaker: tam
nodes.text: Here. Mum's Moomoo Milk, for helping. Two, because there's two of us. Don't tell Lettie I gave you hers.

nodes.speaker: tam

nodes.speaker: cassius
nodes.text: Quiet. Down. ...You came up through the birches. Walked soft, did you? Good.

nodes.speaker: cassius
nodes.text: Cassius Rook. Eleven seasons I've sat up there for the Tilpey Hart. My father sat for it before me, and his father. I've seen it four times. Never close.

nodes.speaker: cassius
nodes.text: It beds down somewhere near. I can smell it, some mornings.

responses.text: Tell him about the hollow down the slope.

nodes.speaker: cassius
nodes.text: A Sawsbuck. Old as the wood. Antlers like a winter tree with the leaves still on. My grandfather swore it was the same one he saw as a boy. I stopped arguing with him about it, and he's been dead twenty years.

nodes.speaker: cassius
nodes.text: Three Rooks have sat for it. If I bring it home in a ball, I'm the last. I can come down off that seat and do something else with my mornings.

nodes.speaker: cassius
nodes.text: ...I don't know what, mind. That's the trouble with it.

nodes.speaker: cassius
nodes.text: ...The hollow. Down the slope, south-east. Under the white birches.

nodes.speaker: cassius
nodes.text: I've walked past that hollow a hundred times. Too obvious. No Rook would ever look there.

nodes.speaker: cassius
nodes.text: Thank you. I'll go down at first light. ...Or the next. There's no hurry, after eleven seasons.

nodes.speaker: cassius
nodes.text: First light, I said. Tomorrow's first light. It'll keep.

nodes.speaker: cassius
nodes.text: Nothing. Aye. Same as me, eleven seasons running.

nodes.speaker: cassius
nodes.text: Don't look sorry for me. A man wants a reason to be up early, and it's a good reason.

nodes.speaker: cassius
nodes.text: Nothing again this morning. Lovely morning for it, though.

nodes.speaker: perrin
nodes.text: Mind the line. Not the road, the line: east of you, the little trees. People cut across and I lose a year under a boot.

nodes.speaker: perrin
nodes.text: Perrin Hale. I count. Don't smile. Somebody has to, and everyone who would rather do something else is busy.

nodes.speaker: perrin
nodes.text: Ask, then. I'm not going anywhere, and neither is she, not quickly.

responses.text: Why do the trees point at the world tree?
What is at the far end of the lane?
Where would I find a Sitrus Berry off the roots?

nodes.speaker: perrin
nodes.text: Years. Thirteen of them, and the paces she's made in each. Eight, near enough. Every spring she gets up, walks eight paces and sits down again, and every spring there's a seedling where she sat.

nodes.speaker: perrin
nodes.text: The stakes are mine; they say the year and what I made of it. The trees are hers. I only keep the lane open, so the little ones get some light.

nodes.speaker: perrin
nodes.text: She's a Grotle. She was a Grotle when I first saw her and she'll be a Grotle when I'm gone, if I'm any judge. Thirty-two makes a Torterra, and she's nowhere near caring.

nodes.speaker: perrin
nodes.text: Gentle, mind. But she's old and she's big, and she'll get up if you walk on her moss. Don't make her do it twice.

nodes.speaker: perrin
nodes.text: The old women say whatever sapling a Grotle holds when she grows up is the tree she wears. Oak, birch, spruce. I've never seen it. I'd like to, and I know I won't.

nodes.speaker: perrin
nodes.text: Because that's where she's going. She set out the spring after the big wind, and I ran a line from her first hollow to the trunk, and she has not drifted off it in thirteen years.

nodes.speaker: perrin
nodes.text: A hundred and seventy paces still to go, near enough. Twenty-two years, at her rate. I'll be ninety-odd. So I write the years on posts, and when I can't, somebody will find the posts.

nodes.speaker: perrin
nodes.text: I haven't been under the tree's roots in nine years. The knee. I used to take a Sitrus Berry off them every autumn, just to know it was still bearing. If you've been under there and you've one on you, show me. I'd like to see one more.

nodes.speaker: perrin
nodes.text: The pole? It's so the tree can see her coming. ...Don't look at me like that. I know what a tree can see. But I light the lantern every dusk, and if she lifts her head from the long walk, there it is: a light, ahead of her, where she's headed.

nodes.speaker: perrin
nodes.text: Climb it if you like. The platform's sound and I oiled the ladder. You'll see the whole lane from up there, and the tree at the end of it. I went up every morning till the knee.

nodes.speaker: perrin
nodes.text: The first stake. Year nought. There's an oak there, the oldest, and a tin I buried under it the spring she set out. I've not dug it up. You may, if you've the legs for a hundred paces. Take what you like; I've no use for what's in it.

nodes.speaker: perrin
nodes.text: At the tree's west foot, where the road goes under the crown. Between the great roots, half grown into them. Go and look; they're not shy about it.

nodes.speaker: perrin
nodes.text: Sitrus. Off the roots? ...Hold it up. There. Still firm, still that smell.

nodes.speaker: perrin
nodes.text: Then it's bearing. Nine years I've wondered. That's... thank you. That's a good thing to know on a long walk.

nodes.speaker: perrin
nodes.text: Here. What she leaves on the lane, dried and sifted: mulch. Put it under a berry tree and the tree will thank you for it. I've more than I can use.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: Mind the fences, they're new. Well, newer than the trees.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: Tamsin Hollin. My mother put in the first row, red, because red is what a Poke Ball wants. Then somebody asked for blue, and somebody else for black, and now there are seven.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: Pick them once they've coloured all the way through. A green one gives you nothing for the trouble.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: And don't pull the branch about. Take the fruit and it grows back where it hung, a quarter of an hour or so, as long as somebody's about to keep it company. Trees don't grow when nobody's looking. Mother swore to that.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: Leave the leaves, too. Every apricorn hangs off one leaf, and if the leaf goes, the fruit goes with it.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: One pick in ten or so you'll find a sprout in with the fruit. Plant it where you like. Not in my rows.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: Four reds round a bit of copper makes four Poke Balls. Blue and red round iron for Great Balls, black and yellow round gold for Ultras. It's on the wall inside if you forget.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: If an apricorn looks back at you, it isn't one. The round ones come for the trees. They mostly just sit there. Mostly.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: The stall on the avenue sells the wood. The fruit's free: there's more on those trees than I'll ever get to.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: Apricorns keep to themselves. Berries don't: plant two kinds side by side and now and then one bears a fruit that's neither. Plant that, and it does it again.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: Mother followed that four summers for the one at the end. Whatever she baited with it, she said, left twice as much behind.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: Pick what's ripe and shut the gates behind you.

nodes.speaker: farmer
nodes.text: Arrow Creeks Farm. Shut the gates behind you. The Wooloo think every open one was opened for them.

nodes.speaker: farmer
nodes.text: The Miltank give the milk, but a Miltank only lets the trainer it belongs to milk it. Bring your own and a bucket. These ones give to the farm and nobody else.

nodes.speaker: farmer
nodes.text: Shears work on the flock, if they'll stand for you. Leave them on the grass afterwards and the fleece comes back.

nodes.speaker: farmer

nodes.speaker: farmer
nodes.text: Milk, wool, leather, honey, eggs: the stand by the south gate sells what we don't use. The Bouffalant pulls the plough and the Ponyta pulls the cart. Neither will pull for you.

nodes.speaker: farmer
nodes.text: Shears for the flock, a bottle for the hives, coin at the stand. And the gates.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: Pull the hide across behind you. The cold follows anyone in.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: I'm Maren. My mother kept the keep on the Strand, and hers before her. Wardenhold. You'll have seen the spire.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: We were forty-one. We kept the yard, the stores, the old log. Nobody lit the beacon. Nobody had to.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: Last winter something came down off the ice and lay down in our yard. Huge. Shadow for legs, gold across its back.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: The cold came off it like smoke. The north-east tower split in a night. Then the roof went, and a turret.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: We dug in here, across the col, where we can still see the spire. Thirty-eight of us made it.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: It's still there. Asleep, mostly. We want our home back.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: Old Sef calls it Giratina, out of his grandmother's stories. The one that lives on the wrong side of things. I don't care what it's called.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: It's strong. Sef says don't go near it with a team that hasn't beaten most of the leaders, and Sef is usually right.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: Through the gate and keep to the middle of the yard. It lies in the east half, on the ice, by the tower that fell.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: Walk up to it and it wakes. Beat it, then come back and tell me.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: You beat it? ...It'll be back. Things like that come back.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: These were lying in the yard where it sleeps. Sef says they belong to it. A core and an orb. Better in your pack than ours.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: If it comes back and you've the strength, take it with you. Then it's yours to worry about.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: We'll go home in the spring. Watch the spire for a fire.

nodes.speaker: sef
nodes.text: Sit. The fire's the only warm thing down here.

nodes.speaker: sef
nodes.text: The Wardens' log says the shelf used to answer the fire. Nobody answers now.

nodes.speaker: sef
nodes.text: That thing in the yard, my grandmother had a name for it. Giratina. Banished, she said, to the back of the world. Seems it got out.

nodes.speaker: sef
nodes.text: It doesn't eat. It doesn't hunt. It just lies there, and the world goes thin round it.

nodes.speaker: sef
nodes.text: Mind the hearth.

nodes.speaker: sef
nodes.text: You fought it? Then you've seen the dark under it. Sit closer to the fire.

nodes.speaker: pell
nodes.text: I keep the count. Forty-one went out the gate. Thirty-eight came here. It's on the wall.

nodes.speaker: pell
nodes.text: We dug all of this with the keep's own picks. Twelve nights for the hall alone.

nodes.speaker: pell
nodes.text: The stores are south. Don't bother with the barrels, they're mostly empty.

nodes.speaker: pell
nodes.text: Still no fire on the spire.

nodes.speaker: pell
nodes.text: You went in the yard and came back out? Can I tell the others? I'm telling the others.
